brief: A Market Ear chart roundup compiles cross-asset stress readings from several desks. Marlin notes the VIX's weekly spike ranks fifth-largest in history, just behind the GFC, COVID, the Flash Crash and Liberation Day. Steno flags oil's 2-week 'all-in-barrel' move as a new record, bigger than the GFC or COVID. GS's vol desk reports gold's 3-month 25-delta skew and implied volatility hit 4-5 standard deviation moves on November 20th, a multiyear skew high. Marquee notes a BTC volatility spike, while FX and bond vol stay calm by comparison. GS's trading desk flags S&P futures top-of-book depth near four-year lows just as liquidity is needed most. Against this panic, Jefferies argues history favors buyers: VIX 20-30 forward returns are uninspiring, but above 30 the picture improves, and above 35 average 12-month returns have exceeded 20%. GBM notes Goldman's US Vol Panic Index at 9.2/10, where readings above 9.5 have historically signaled near-term relief. Bilello adds that the VIX sits in the highest 5% of readings since 1990, and buying equities at such fear levels has historically delivered stronger long-term returns than calmer-market buying, though panic can deepen further and the historical average is no guarantee.
